title: Describing and Understanding Pacing Strategies during Athletic Competition
claims: Pacing profiles in competition are commonly described as negative, all-out, positive, even, parabolic or variable according to how speed or pace unfolds across the event.

For prolonged events lasting more than about two minutes, performance generally benefits from an even distribution of effort rather than an early surge, and fatigue regulation is central to maintaining pace.
Well-trained ultra-endurance runners often adopt a positive pacing profile that peaks early and slows gradually through the latter part of the event.
